model.name: DREAM S2 semantic news-cycle retention
model.lambda_interpretation: lambda = elapsed hours since semantic topic attention peak
model.abstraction_layer: Raw RSS articles are converted into stable semantic topic objects before S2 fitting.
model.semantic_layer: Sparse TF-IDF article vectors, entity sets, keyword distributions, semantic connected components, centroid inertia, and a persistent topic_memory.json file.
model.event_horizon_layer: H(t)=Deviation(t)*CrossScaleCoherence(t), with Deviation=observed/expected_S2 and CrossScaleCoherence from source-tier spread, source diversity, and semantic coherence. Pre-horizon alerts require high H and positive slope.
model.signal_preprocessing: Formal S2 fit uses circadian-corrected publish-time article counts: raw count divided by expected global publishing/activity factor.
model.observation_clock: article.published_at, not GitHub Action run time
model.history_role: data/history.json retains raw article records and first_seen/last_seen provenance; topic_memory.json retains semantic identity; cycles.json retains completed S2 cycle summaries.
model.comparison: Delta AIC = AIC(exponential beta=1) - AIC(stretched S2 beta free)
model.cycle_archive_role: data/cycles.json stores deduplicated completed formal cycle summaries so prior S2 learning remains visible when a new wave resets the current topic. Current waves are not archived until replaced by a new peak.

articles.title: Trump administration finalizes rule to end federal support for gender-affirming care
articles.summary: Move blocking funds through Medicaid and Chip to make it harder for vulnerable children to get healthcare, experts say The Trump administration finalized a rule on Tuesday to end gender-affirming care through Medicaid and the Children’s Health Insurance Program (Chip), a move that will make it harder for vulnerable children to access healthcare and that eschews evidence to advance an anti-transgender ideology, opponents say. The rule is set to take effect on 13 October – but legal challenges could delay or block it entirely. Continue reading...

articles.title: How Trump’s order on vaccines is sowing confusion, doubt and fear
articles.summary: The order cannot affect change, and is only ‘undermining trust in vaccines’ as CDC guidance remains the same Donald Trump’s executive order on vaccines does not change the US recommendations for the shots – but experts say it does create confusion and doubt about vaccines, which will lead to more illness and possibly deaths among children and will make it harder for families and pediatricians to protect them. The executive order was an attempt to reinstate sweeping changes to the vaccine schedule made earlier this year by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services and a longtime vaccine opponent – changes that were later halted by a federal judge.
